failureRemedy.limit_exceeded: Narrow the request to one goal, or split it into two shorter tasks — this one ran out of budget before it finished.
failureRemedy.timed_out: Try again when the site is responding normally, or break the request into smaller steps so each one finishes inside the limit.
failureRemedy.timeout: Ask for a smaller slice of the work, then continue from where it stopped.
failureRemedy.enqueue_failed: Nothing reached the browser worker. Wait a moment and try again; if it keeps happening, the browser service is down.
failureRemedy.blocked: The site refused automation. Open the page yourself and check for a policy notice, or use an account that is allowed to do this.
failureRemedy.proxy_failure: Check your network, then try again. A VPN or corporate proxy is the usual cause.
failureRemedy.model_refusal: Reword the request so the intent is explicit, and avoid asking for actions the model must refuse.
failureRemedy.captcha_blocked: Take control, clear the CAPTCHA or sign in yourself, then let the task continue.
failureRemedy.page_load_failure: Open the URL yourself and confirm it loads. If it needs a sign-in or is down, fix that first, then try again.
failureRemedy.network_error: Check your connection and try again.
failureRemedy.stalled: No browser picked the task up. Make sure Chrome is open with the Cluega extension connected, then try again.
failureRemedy.browser_auth_expired: Send the request again and approve the browser prompt as soon as it appears.
failureRemedy.browser_auth_rejected: Send the request again and choose Allow when asked for browser access.
failureRemedy.connector_disabled: Turn My Browser back on in Connect apps, then send the request again.
failureRemedy.stuck: The page did not respond the way the task expected. Take control to get past the step, or describe that step explicitly in your request.
failureRemedy.partial: Look at what came back, then ask for just the missing part rather than re-running the whole task.
failureRemedy.unknown: Try again. If it fails the same way twice, send the task id to support — there is no user-side fix for this one.
failureRemedy.lane_wait_expired: Your browser was busy with another task. Wait for that one to finish (or stop it), then try again.
failureRemedy.target_not_found: The page layout changed. Try again so the task reads the page fresh; if it keeps missing, name the button or field in your request.
failureRemedy.stale_observation: The page was still loading or re-rendering. Try again once it has settled.
failureRemedy.popup_obscured: Take control and close the dialog, cookie banner or overlay, then let the task continue.
failureRemedy.tab_changed: Leave the driven tab in the foreground while the task runs, then try again.
failureRemedy.duplicate_action: Check whether the action already went through before running it again — repeating it may double the result.
failureRemedy.click_no_effect: The control did nothing when clicked. Take control to check the page, or name a different route to the same goal in your request.
failureRemedy.value_not_set: The page rejected the value. Check what that field requires — a minimum, a currency, a format — and state the acceptable value in your request.
failureRemedy.field_not_found: This is not the page rejecting the value: there was no box to type into. Check on the open page when that field appears (some only appear once clicked), then reply and I will rerun.
failureRemedy.debugger_unavailable: Close DevTools on the task tab and keep the tab open, then try again.
failureRemedy.auth_wall: Take control, sign in to the site in that tab, tick "keep me signed in", then try again.
failureRemedy.extension_disconnected: Open Chrome, check the Cluega extension is installed, enabled and showing as connected, then try again.
failureRemedy.require_browser_connection: Connect your browser first, then send the request again.
failureRemedy.permission_denied: Grant the missing permission to the Cluega desktop app (screen recording and accessibility are the usual ones), then try again.
failureRemedy.runtime_offline: Start the Cluega Desktop app and wait until it shows as connected, then try again.
failureRemedy.driver_error: Try again. If it repeats, restart the Cluega Desktop app.
failureRemedy.app_launch_failed: Open the app manually once and confirm it starts, then try again.
failureRemedy.window_changed: Leave the app window in the foreground while the task runs, then try again.
failureRemedy.risk_blocked: This step spends money or cannot be undone, so Cluega will not take it alone. Take control and do it yourself, or say explicitly in your request that you authorize it.
failureRemedy.user_declined: Send the request again and approve the step, or reword it so that step is not needed.
failureRemedy.confirm_timeout: Send the request again and answer the confirmation prompt when it appears.
failureRemedy.unsupported_action: This environment cannot do that action. Try it in your own browser, or ask for a different route to the same result.
failureRemedy.account_choice_required: Say which account to use — put the account name in your request — and it will continue without asking.
failureRemedy.account_choice_ambiguous: Two accounts share that name. Give the account id, or something else that tells them apart.
failureRemedy.relay_unavailable: The link to your browser dropped. Check Chrome is still open with the extension connected, then try again.
failureRemedy.gateway_unreachable: The AI service could not be reached. Wait a moment and try again.
failureRemedy.step_limit_exceeded: The task ran out of steps. Ask for a smaller piece of the work, then continue from where it stopped.
failureRemedy.observation_timeout: The browser did not report back in time. Try again; if it repeats, close heavy tabs so Chrome has room to respond.
failureRemedy.brain_unavailable: The decision service did not answer. Wait a moment and try again.
failureRemedy.no_progress: The page stopped changing. Take control to see where it is stuck, or name the next step explicitly in your request.
failureRemedy.loop_detected: The task kept repeating itself. Describe the steps you want in order, so it has a route instead of guessing.
failureRemedy.ask_timeout: Cluega asked you for a value and got no answer in time. Send the request again and reply when it asks.
failureRemedy.user_step_required: Finish that step in the open page yourself, then reply here and Cluega will carry on.
failureRemedy.plan_unfinished: Part of the plan was never started. Ask for just the remaining part rather than re-running everything.
failureRemedy.user_stopped: Nothing went wrong. Reply here when you want Cluega to carry on from where it stopped.
failureRemedy.platform_rate_limited: Cluega did not switch account, retry or split the request. Wait for the limit to lift, then confirm to continue.
failureRemedy.account_restricted: Cluega did not switch account, retry or split the request. Check the account's status on the platform, then confirm to continue.
failureRemedy.account_locked: Check the account on the platform, then confirm it is fine so the hold is lifted.
failureRemedy.risky_site: Ask again and name a source you trust, or tell Cluega which site to use instead.
failureRemedy.device_wait_expired: Open Chrome with the Cluega extension on your computer, then try again.
failureRemedy.unsupported_browser: Open Cluega in Google Chrome on your computer, with the Cluega extension, and run the task there.
failureRemedy.password_field_refused: Take control, type the password or code yourself, then hand back so the task can carry on.
failureRemedy.skill_broken: Record the skill again so it follows the site as it is now.
failureRemedy.sandbox_unavailable: Open the bot's computer to wake it, then try again.
failureRemedy.unsupported_sandbox_screen: Give the task to the bot on the computer's main screen, or move this bot to its own computer.
failureRemedy.skill_target_mismatch: Run the skill where it was recorded, or record it again here.
failureRemedy.unsupported_sandbox_step: Run this skill in Cluega in Chrome, or record it again without the upload step.
failureRemedy.app_not_installed: Ask the bot in chat to install the app (it will ask you to confirm), then run the skill again.

prompts.title: Prompts
prompts.subtitle: The most practical prompts — copy and paste into Cluega. Replace everything in [] brackets with your own details.

audit.title: Account health audit
audit.body: Pull audit of all Google Ads accounts. Flag the top 5 issues ranked by estimated $ impact. IS lost to budget vs. rank, QS-weighted underperformers, conversion-tracking gaps (<10 conv / 7 days), assets below 'Good' ad strength, and broad-match spend where STRs don't match intent. For each: wasted spend last 30d + expected ROAS uplift if fixed.

weeklyDiagnosis.title: Week-over-week diagnosis
weeklyDiagnosis.body: Compare last 7 days vs. prior 7 across all Google Ads campaigns. Surface biggest deltas in ROAS, CPA, IS, avg CPC. For each: primary driver (auction pressure, CTR, LP conv rate, pacing, specific keyword/ad), and whether it's seasonal noise or a real shift. Isolate brand vs. non-brand so brand doesn't mask the picture.

topOpportunities.title: Top 3 opportunities
topOpportunities.body: Top 10 optimization opportunities across Google + Meta, ranked by estimated $/month impact. For each: (1) lever (budget shift, bid strategy, creative refresh, audience expansion, negative, LP fix), (2) evidence from last 28d, (3) expected lift range with confidence, (4) exec effort in hours, (5) risk.

negativeKeywords.title: Negative keyword scan
negativeKeywords.body: Pull search-terms report last 30d across all campaigns. Find 20 high-impression, zero/low-conversion queries that don't match buyer intent — include wasted spend per term and recommend phrase or exact, at account- or campaign-level. Exclude anything already negated and flag any symmetric negatives I should add to a shared list.

keywordExpansion.title: Keyword expansion
keywordExpansion.body: Based on my top 20 converting search terms last 90d, propose 10-15 new keywords to add. Group into logical ad groups, suggest match type, estimate monthly search volume and competitive bid range, and predict which groups will need new RSAs vs. fit into existing ones. Exclude terms with LP-intent mismatch.

keywordPlanner.title: Keyword Planner (deep dive)
keywordPlanner.body: Run Keyword Planner for '[product/service]' in [country, language]. Clean table: keyword, avg monthly searches, competition, low/high TopP bid, YoY seasonality. Group into 3-5 themes I can build ad groups from. Flag any high-volume terms where competition suggests retargeting-only instead of prospecting.

hourly.title: An hourly monitoring centre that leaves data anomalies nowhere to hide
hourly.body: Build hourly reports freely by platform, ad account, campaign or ad group, and merge several objects into one view with a single click. Set your own columns and condition rules; the moment something goes wrong an email or Pulse notification goes out with links straight to the detail and its report, so you catch the problem first and react fast.

master.title: Big Report: one platform, every account, one table
master.body: Create one Big Report per platform, merge several ad accounts into it and let time zones convert automatically, so accounts stay comparable. Inside the report you can switch between Pivot and the trend dashboard, combining dimensions and metrics freely. Creatives can carry tags and an assigned owner, so it is obvious who owns what. Once hourly monitoring is set, spend or performance outside your thresholds will notify you. Every CPA here is internal cost (spend ÷ conversions), not a client quote.

optimizer.title: Optimizer report — performance attributed to people, at a glance
optimizer.body: Performance is attributed to each optimizer automatically by delivery attribution, then seat reassignment, then account default, with spend, conversions and CPA rolled up across Meta / TikTok / Google. Open any optimizer to see their account detail and deep-link straight into the matching master report.

label.title: Label report — break real data out through a project lens
label.body: Tag an ad group and that tag becomes a project, splitting out real spend, conversions and CPA by label. The label list gives you the rollup; pick any label to drill into account detail with its optimizer attached. Add and search labels freely and switch between projects to compare.
features: Labels are projects, split from real data
Label list rolls up spend / conversions / CPA
Drill into account detail with its optimizer

attribution.title: Attribution comparison — recover the true CPA
attribution.body: Platform-reported conversions rarely match the third party, so pair a third-party attribution source per pixel/app to recover the real CPA. All three delivery APIs sync every pixel and app automatically — nothing to maintain by hand — and days whose gap passes your threshold are flagged, with match rate tracked alongside.
features: Pair a third-party source, recover the true CPA
Automatic sync across all three delivery APIs
Days over the threshold are flagged

creative.title: Creatives deduplicated across identities — real performance surfaces
creative.body: Creatives merge across identities automatically, so the same creative running under several handles still counts once and the numbers never inflate. Key metrics sit together, hourly/daily switching is built in, and everything can be exported or shared.

creativeLabels.title: Label-driven creative attribution and lifecycle insight — repeat the hits, see the decline coming
creativeLabels.body: Every running creative is classified by label automatically, with spend, conversions and CPA aggregated live. A lifecycle wave chart traces each creative from ramp-up through breakout to decline, so you spot the fade early and top up or replace in time.

product.title: Three conversion sources side by side — the product-dimension report shows what really happened
product.body: A product's domains and app links trace spend back to the accounts that owned it, then plot platform, third-party and product-backend conversions side by side on one timeline — where the peaks stop lining up is your anomaly signal. Drill any report down to pixel, source account and CPA detail, and compute gross margin live from your own multiplier.
features: Gross margin on your own multiplier

custom.title: Start from a blank canvas — stack any dimensions and metrics into the report you want
custom.body: No preset template. Frame the data scope and timezone first, then stack as many dimensions as you like from ad account, campaign, ad group, creative, label and product — the first dimension sets the report's row level. Metrics come from the shared metric registry so definitions stay consistent. Pick at least one of each and the report is yours.
features: Your own data scope and timezone

chapters.title: Master, optimizer and label in one place — switch report lists as you read
chapters.body: Pick a report chapter and the list of reports you already have appears underneath, so there is no jumping between three separate places to find them.

deliver.manualBody: The classic form flow — campaign, ad group and ad, all set by you. Domain, age, region and country are **filled in from the account**, with batch launch and reusable strategy templates.
deliver.manualBox: Entirely your way, no automatic decisions
deliver.manualCaption: Can be saved as a template
deliver.remember: Remember my choice: next time on this platform, go straight to the selected mode. Resettable in settings.

product.step2: Choose delivery links and match pixels

product.step3Hint: Same custom-columns modal as the Master Report, plus product data pipelines
product.filterFields: Filter fields (same as Master custom columns)

head.marketUnknown: No market set on the product

gaps.not_in_registry: This metric is not in the server's field registry yet, so there is no number to read. Both inputs already exist; it needs the formula adding.
gaps.no_source: D7 ROAS needs cohort data — revenue on day 7 from the users who installed on day 0. Every source we have reports revenue within the window instead, which is a different number, so no approximation is shown in its place.

split.title: Spend share by platform
split.subtitle: Every source account under the same attribution app token
split.measuredOnlyNote: The bar shows share of MEASURED spend, not share of budget. Only TikTok can attribute spend at pixel grain, so {platforms} spend is in neither this chart nor the total above. For a figure that includes them, use the master report.
split.allMeasuredNote: Every pixel on this product is measurable, so the bar's shares are shares of the total spend.
split.residualWarning: The platform slices add up to {measured}, which disagrees with the total spend {total} above (off by {residual}). Both come from the same payload, so a difference means reconciliation failed — do not quote this chart, and report this report id.
split.spendNotCounted: spend not counted in the total
split.noData: No data landed for this window
split.noDataHint: This platform does support pixel-grain measurement and the pixel is bound, but the source reported nothing. Check that the ad account is authorised and that there really was delivery in this window.
split.noDataNote: {platforms} pixels are bound and pixel-grain measurement is supported, but nothing landed for this window, so they are absent from the bar. This is a data problem — authorisation, sync, or genuinely no delivery — not a missing feature.

crossCheck.title: Attribution cross-check
crossCheck.bodyApp: The gap is the change in {mmp} installs relative to the platform's reported conversions. Cross-platform double attribution and click-window differences both produce one; the MMP normally counts fewer than the platform.
crossCheck.bodyWeb: The gap is the change in third-party conversions relative to the platform's reported conversions. This product's targets are all websites, so there is no install event to compare.
crossCheck.denominatorNote: What “platform-reported conversions” counts depends on each ad group’s optimisation goal — install-optimised groups report installs, payment-optimised ones report payments. This report cannot read those goals, so it cannot tell which of them the range covers: read the gap as a direction, not as a reconciliation.
crossCheck.notComparable: At least one side was not measured, so no gap can be computed.
crossCheck.gapUndefined: The platform reported zero conversions, so the gap is undefined — not 0%.

tree.title: Account · Campaign · Ad group
tree.subtitle: Click to expand; every figure is summed up from the ad groups
tree.mmpColumnsNote: This table carries platform-side figures only. Installs, payments and third-party ROAS are reported by the attribution provider per DELIVERY LINK and have no ad-group grain; splitting them across ad groups would be apportionment, so they are not offered here — see the KPI row and the link table above.
tree.sumNote: Every tier equals the sum of the tier below it. That is this table's own guarantee.
tree.disagreesTitle: This table disagrees with the total spend above
tree.disagreesBody: This table totals {tree}; the KPI row above says {report}. They come from two different ad-platform routes: the KPI row from the captured hourly data, this table from the daily data. A day still syncing produces exactly this difference. For reconciliation use the KPI row; use this table to read the structure.
tree.failedAdvertisers: These ad accounts could not be read, so their ad groups are absent: {accounts}
tree.truncated: The read hit its page bound, so this table is a lower bound — there may be ad groups not listed.
tree.silentAdgroups: {n} ad groups reported nothing in this window. They are still listed, with blank cells — blank means unmeasured, not zero.
tree.empty: No delivery structure to show. Either this report has no pixels selected, the selected pixels have no ad accounts bound, or nothing was delivered in this window.
tree.unsupported: The delivery structure is read live from the ad platform, and a shared page carries no credential for that — so it is not shown.

creativeTab.title: Creative performance
creativeTab.subtitle: Only creatives under this product's ad groups, with figures narrowed to them
creativeTab.shareNote: These {n} creatives account for {share} of this product's spend.
creativeTab.coverageNote: The material report covers only ads that HAVE an asset, so the creative total ({creative}) is normally below the product's spend ({product}). The {gap} difference is delivery with no linked asset — expected, not missing data.
creativeTab.unavailableNote: These columns do not exist at creative grain and are not offered: {columns}. Installs and CPI are reported by the attribution provider per delivery link, with no creative grain; D7 ROAS needs cohort data. The ROAS in this table is the platform's own, within the window.
creativeTab.empty: No creative data under this product's ad groups for this window.
creativeTab.needsTree: The creative table needs the delivery structure — the ad group list — to narrow its scope. When that is unavailable above, this table cannot be shown either.
creativeTab.partial: Some ad accounts could not be read; this table is a lower bound.

audienceTab.filtersDisabled: The filters need audience dimensions to act on, and there is none to filter.
audienceTab.overviewReason: All four need TikTok's AUDIENCE report dimensions (age, gender, country_code, province_id, interest_category). Our delivery sync covers only advertiser / campaign / ad group / ad, and no level carries these fields — so there is no approximation to show instead.
audienceTab.engageReason: App opens and session length are product-side behavioural data — they come from the product's own backend or the MMP's event stream, not from the ad platform. That pipeline is not connected.
audienceTab.engageHint: Ad-level video engagement (play rate, completion rate) IS available — but that is creative performance, not audience behaviour, so it lives in the Creative tab and is deliberately not folded in here.
audienceTab.interestReason: The hashtag ranking comes from TikTok's Creative Center; interest coverage and interest-package spend come from the AUDIENCE dimensions. Neither is connected.
audienceTab.deviceTitle: Device OS · OS version · Device price
audienceTab.deviceReason: Also needs the AUDIENCE dimensions (platform, os_version, device_price).
audienceTab.detailReason: This table breaks down by age / gender / device OS, needing the same dimensions as above.
audienceTab.whatWouldUnblock: What would unblock it: an AUDIENCE report sync in ad_manager. The upstream API already supports report_type=AUDIENCE, and a sibling system (sh-adwise) already syncs these dimensions. It needs ad_manager's maintainer to take it on.

finance.tableNote: Top-up − spend − balance must net to zero; only then is the loop closed. Untagged accounts are listed separately and a non-zero difference flags red.

complianceFix.title: Fix to compliant
complianceFix.intro: Edits this creative's content to meet the policy TikTok cited, so you can resubmit it for review. It changes what the video shows and says; it does not try to get around review.
complianceFix.whyRejected: Why TikTok did not approve it
complianceFix.noReason: TikTok returned no reason text for this creative.
complianceFix.plannedChanges: What the fix will change (content only)
complianceFix.doneChanges: What this version changed, and why

change.restrictedAudience: Makes the video suitable for adults only: removes anything that appeals to children or teenagers and adds a clear 18+ notice — TikTok restricts this product category to 18+ audiences.
change.claims: Removes claims that cannot be substantiated (earnings, winnings, guaranteed results, superlatives, before-and-after, fake buttons) from the on-screen text and voice-over, and describes the product factually instead.
change.sensitive: Cuts the sensitive shots entirely and replaces them with neutral product shots — they are removed, not blurred or cropped.
change.intellectualProperty: Replaces third-party music, logos and footage you do not own with original or royalty-free material.
change.quality: Re-renders the video cleanly: full frame, sharp, no black frames, watermarks or cut-off text.
change.language: Makes on-screen text and captions consistent, in one language that matches the voice-over and the target market.
change.other: Reworks the elements TikTok objected to, following its suggestion, while keeping the product and message.

complianceFix.targetingNote: TikTok also requires a setting the video cannot change: set this ad group's age targeting to 18+ (ad group → targeting → age) before resubmitting.
complianceFix.notFixable: TikTok does not allow this product to be advertised here, so no edit of the video would pass. Use another creative from the library instead.
complianceFix.useLibrary: Use another creative from the library
complianceFix.failedFallback: No compliant version could be generated this time. You can use another creative from the library instead.
complianceFix.resultNote: New compliant version generated. It is not on the ad and nothing was sent to TikTok: add it to the library, then swap it in with «Replace from library», which resubmits the ad for review.
complianceFix.verdictNote: Whether it passes is TikTok's decision when it is reviewed again.

reason.execute_failed: The platform call didn't complete — its state is unknown.
reason.kernel_error: Something went wrong before the change was sent.
reason.run_already_waiting: This conversation already has a run open for that, and waiting won't clear it. Finish the card above, or cancel it and ask again.

SHOPIFY.title: Install with the TikTok app for Shopify
steps: Open the TikTok app in your Shopify admin and connect your TikTok For Business account.
Under Data sharing, choose this pixel and turn on Maximum (browser pixel + Events API).
Save. Shopify sends the standard events for you.

GTM.title: Install with Google Tag Manager
steps: Add the TikTok Pixel template from the Community Template Gallery.
Paste this pixel code into the tag and fire it on All Pages.
Add one tag per event, then submit and publish the container.

MANUAL.title: Paste the code on your site
steps: Copy the pixel base code from TikTok Events Manager.
Paste it inside <head> on every page of your site.
Add the event code on product, cart and checkout pages.
